title: Event Sanitizer and Backpressure Gateway for Usage Streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Replace the brittle, synchronous schema gate at the telemetry edge with a resilient Event Sanitizer + Backpressure Gateway (ESBG) that performs: canonicalization, permissive validation (with configurable strictness per customer), efficient rejection-fallbacks, and adaptive backpressure to preserve platform SLOs.

Background: Our current ingest pipeline frequently causes tail-latency spikes when malformed or unexpectedly large events hit the validator. During bursts this leads to timeouts that cascade into higher retry traffic and customer-visible errors. We need a gateway that keeps the happy path fast, enables safe schema evolution, and captures bad/unknown events for later analysis without blocking healthy traffic.

Scope:
- Gateway service (Go) deployed in front of the event queue (Kafka topic: usage-events.raw).
- JSON -> canonicalized form conversion (normalize timestamps, canonicalize model identifiers, trim large free-text fields).
- Fast validation against JSON Schema v7 with an allowlist mode and "per-field sanitizer" hooks for common corruption patterns.
- Adaptive backpressure: token-bucket/circuit-breaker per upstream partition/customer that switches validation to "best-effort" mode and routes failures to blobstore when thresholds exceeded.
- Reject-to-blobstore flow: rejected/ambiguous events go to a write-only bucket (GCS) with metadata for replay and manual review.
- Schema drift detector: lightweight metrics emitted when unknown fields appear or validation pass rates change by >3% over a 1h window.
- Observability: per-customer metrics (ingest rate, validation latency p50/p95/p99, rejection rate, blobstore spill rate), dashboards, and alerting.

Architectural decisions made so far:
- Use Go for the gateway (existing infra, low-allocation JSON parsing benefits).
- Use https://github.com/xeipuuv/gojsonschema for initial validation; wrap in a small adapter to allow future replacement with a WASM-based validator.
- Rejected events are batched and written to GCS with a compact manifest JSON containing validation errors and original event hash. Blob URIs are surfaced to a replay tool.
- For low-latency customers (dedicated tiers), validation level will be configurable per-API-key, allowing stricter or laxer rules.
- Circuit-breaker policy: if validation p99 > 150ms or rejection rate > 1% for 5m, flip to best-effort and emit an incident telemetry event.

Acceptance criteria:
- Happy-path add <3ms median CPU processing overhead for validated events at typical size distribution (payloads < 2KB).
- For synthetic burst tests (x5 baseline throughput), gateway must keep end-to-end success rate >= 99% by degrading validation gracefully (spill to GCS allowed).
- All rejected events are accessible via replay UI (link in docs) with stored validation errors.
- Dashboards for validation latency and rejection rates deployed to Grafana; at least one alert on rising rejection-rate trend.
- End-to-end integration test in CI that injects malformed event types and asserts they land in GCS with expected metadata.

Implementation plan / milestones:
1) Prototype validator wrapper + canonicalizer library (spike) — owner: Marco — due 2025-02-21.
2) Gateway service core (validation, canonicalization, routing to Kafka/GCS) — due 2025-03-04.
3) Backpressure & circuit-breaker logic + per-customer config — due 2025-03-10.
4) Observability, dashboards, and alerting — due 2025-03-12.
5) Staged rollout (canary on 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100%) with auto-rollback on defined SLO violations — target completion 2025-03-15.

Testing and QA:
- Synthetic generator: add new workload generator that can produce schema-variant events and corruption patterns (null bytes, truncated JSON, huge text fields).
- Load tests: run at 3x and 5x baseline in staging; verify spill and degrade behavior.
- Fuzz tests against canonicalizer and sanitizer functions to surface crashes and unexpected panics.

Open design questions / trade-offs:
- Strictness model: whether to support per-field auto-correction (e.g., coerce integers stored as strings) vs. always rejecting. Current leaning: provide opt-in autocorrections in a configurable policy to avoid silent data corruption.
- Storage path for replays: GCS chosen for immediate MVP; long-term we may stream rejected events into a different Kafka topic for nearline reprocessing.
- Validation library: gojsonschema is quick to integrate but may be slower at p99 than WASM-based, consider migration if p99 validation latency > 150ms.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Event+Sanitizer+Design
- Spike repo + proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/tree/feature/event-sanitizer-spike
- WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6789
- Replay tool prototype (internal): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cExample/view
- Staging dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/validation-overview

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: validator adds CPU cost that raises overall cost-per-token. Mitigation: offload heavy validation to best-effort path and implement sampling + adaptive validation.
- Risk: schema changes may be missed if we over-tolerate new fields. Mitigation: schema drift detector and daily drift reports to product/PMs.
- Risk: replay and GCS storage could accumulate large volumes. Mitigation: lifecycle policy (30d cold storage) and size-based sampling for extremely noisy customers.

Next steps (this ticket):
- Complete prototype canonicalizer and submit PR for review (PR link above).
- Sync with PM (Ivy Chen) on customer strictness defaults and SLAs for dedicated tenants.
- Schedule security review (KMS handling for any PII fields) once MVP code is ready.

Contact: Marco Nguyen (assignee) for engineering questions; Aisha Patel (creator/owner) for product/priority.

2025-02-22: Team decision to use gojsonschema for MVP with adapter layer; performance concern noted for p99. Spike to measure in staging scheduled.
2025-02-28: PR #6789 created with gateway skeleton; CI lint and unit tests green. Requesting initial code review from infra-maintainers.
2025-03-03: Load test at 3x baseline passed with best-effort degrade path; observed validation p99 at ~120ms. Planning backpressure tuning next.
2025-03-04: Security pinged for review; flagged need to redline any PII normalization rules and confirm KMS usage for replay manifests.
